newsitem.title: FRANCE: Scattered storms halt French grain harvest.
newsitem.headline: Scattered storms halt French grain harvest.

text.p: French grain harvesting north of the river Seine was halted by rain on Friday, prompting sellers to withdraw from an already quiet cash market, grain traders said.
Rain in the Paris grain regions had disrupted field work overnight and scattered thundery showers late on Friday stopped the harvest altogether, they said.
One or two flash storms were reported to have been violent with heavy but short bursts of rain.
Traders said there some talk of potential damage to quality and quanity north of Paris.
But there was no suggestion so far that any localized damage had been enough to alter the outlook for what promises to be another large crop this year, especially of feed grain.
The harvest is working its way north and has crossed the river Seine, which runs through Paris, for both wheat and barley.
"The market is stuck. Sellers are playing cautious," one domestic trader said.
Rouen-delivered soft wheat was quoted unchanged at 865 francs per tonne excluding carrying charges for September and October, though August was quoted down a touch at 857.50 francs.
Spot Rouen-delivered feed barley stood at 810 francs and prompt Bordeaux-delivered maize at 835 francs excluding carry.
Carrrying charges are currently 3.34 francs for each half-month between August 1 and the delivery period.

On the export front, markets were caught between a European Union decision to raise taxes and the seemingly unstoppable rise of the dollar -- now worth more than 6.34 francs whereas it had been less than 6.20 francs through most of last week.
The dollar is making European wheat moire attractive and helping to erode the effects of EU export taxes.
Matif soft wheat futures rose in minimal trading by eight francs to 893 francs a tonne for September barge delivery.
